question: Value of refractive index can be calculated by using :
solution:
The correct answer is '__Snell's law__'.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Refraction**: The bending of light or change in the direction of propagation of light as it moves from one medium to another medium is called refraction.
 
• **Snell's law of refraction** states that the **ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence (i) to the sine of the angle of refraction (r) is constant **for a light of a given wavelength travelling in a given pair of media.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/909b91f9667c45d466edf5d87de3c31d3dc1a70e96b3d5b6f7cf872051091c07.png] 

 
• (sin i)/(sim r ) = mu 
 
• Here**, mu\: is the refractive index** of the second medium with respect to the first medium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• According to **Ohm's law**, if the temperature and all other physical factors remain constant, the **voltage across a conductor is directly proportional to the current that is flowing through it**.
 
• Along with the Lorentz force law, **Maxwell's equations, often known as the Maxwell-Heaviside equation**s, are a **set of coupled partial differential equations that serve as the theoretical basis for classical electromagnetism, classical optics, and electric circuits**. They explain how **charges, currents, and field changes cause electric and magnetic fields **to form.
 
• The **relation between an object's motion and the forces acting on it** is outlined by **Newton's laws of motion**, which are three fundamental principles of classical mechanics. They set the **groundwork for classical mechanics** by helping Newton examine and describe the motion of numerous physical objects and systems.
